# Run 14 — Component-0 baseline (Condition A), seed 42

**Status.** Single-seed first scaled run. The first NH-cudalstm run on the
183-basin Component-0 network.

**Model.** NH `cudalstm` + basin ID one-hot encoding. 183 HUC-1 to HUC-6
eastern-US basins (Component 0). 30 epochs. Seed 42.

**Config.** Generated by Cell 7 of `notebooks/colab_publication_run.ipynb`
from `experiments/configs/lstm_component0_baseline.yaml` with
`experiment_name: A_baseline_seed42` and `device: cuda:0`. Trained on
Colab Pro (L4 GPU). Local config has `device` patched to `cpu` for the
post-hoc evaluate step.

**Result.** Median test NSE **0.6480** (mean 0.586). NSE range
[-6.495, 0.851]. The mean is dragged down by a few outlier basins; median
is the robust summary.

**Why it matters.** This is the **load-bearing baseline** for the locked
A/B/C protocol on Component 0 — every graph-variant comparison at scale is
measured against this number. The 0.648 median is substantially higher than
the 23-basin pilot's 0.423 (run 05): **the larger basin set is "easier"**
in the multi-basin LSTM regime, consistent with Kratzert 2019's finding
that more basins → better cross-basin generalization.

**Associated outputs.**
- Per-basin NSE: `test/model_epoch030/test_metrics.csv` (183 rows)
- Full predictions: `test/model_epoch030/test_results.p`
- Training log: `output.log`
- Static-feature scaler + basin-encoding map: `train_data/`

**Where it fits in the project narrative.** Condition A in the locked
A/B/C protocol (`idea1.md` §A/B/C Publication-Run Protocol). Establishes
that Component-0 LSTM-only baseline is in the 0.6-0.7 NSE range — much
higher than the 23-basin pilot. Sets the bar that B (topology features)
and C (graph + messages) must meet to claim a structural-information
contribution.
